clue.text: Awful know-all hogs it — OK, there may be accusation of hypocrisy

definitions.text: there may be accusation of hypocrisy

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters that follow are a mess to be put right

parts.note: the letters of these four words, hyphen and dash ignored

explanation.surface: An insufferable know-all monopolises a conversation, and someone might fairly call them a hypocrite.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is described rather than given: it is the retort you make when someone criticises a fault they share.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a sarcastic rejoinder pointing out that the critic is guilty of the very thing they complain about.

clue.text: Restraint on beloved, heard to be a beast

parts.note: a rein restrains a horse

indicators.note: what is heard is only spoken, so we want a word that sounds like beloved rather than its spelling

parts.note: a beloved person is your dear; 'on' places it after the first piece

explanation.surface: A lover hears that their sweetheart is being held back, and is called a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is a large antlered animal of the Arctic, so it is a beast in the general sense.

clue.text: See 13
Seize part of royal bride's dress

parts.note: Di, Princess Diana, was the famous royal bride of 1981; add the possessive S
the train is the long trailing part of a wedding dress

explanation.surface: An instruction to grab a piece of a princess's wedding gown.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Di's train', Diana's famous long train at her 1981 wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is a legal term meaning to seize goods in settlement of a debt.

clue.text: Monster that is appearing with head on top

indicators.note: in a down answer, what sits on top is written first, above the rest

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A monster shows itself, its head poking up above the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on top' puts the headland above the 'that is' letters. Nessie is the Loch Ness monster of Scottish legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the popular nickname for the Loch Ness Monster, a creature said to live in a Scottish lake.

clue.text: What starts temptation in unlucky OT man — an apple

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: Jonah, the Old Testament prophet, brought bad luck to his ship; a Jonah is a jinx

indicators.note: what starts a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of temptation
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Eden story: what begins temptation for Adam is an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Eden's apple, but the OT man is the prophet blamed for the storm in the Book of Jonah, not Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan is a variety of red eating apple first grown in New York State.

clue.text: Second best? Protest audibly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the cream is the best of something

explanation.surface: Someone who came second complains loudly about not winning.
explanation.definitionFit: To scream is to cry out shrilly, a loud way of making an objection heard.

clue.text: Insects possibly mate in spring, say?

indicators.note: possibly signals one arrangement among several, so the following letters may be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A nature note wondering whether insects breed in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is especially apt: female mantises are notorious for eating their mates.
explanation.definitionFit: Praying mantises are predatory insects named for the way they hold their forelegs as if in prayer.

clue.text: Show agent round when back working

indicators.note: going back means running from end to start, so the preceding letters are read the other way

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
a rep, or representative, acts as an agent
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A theatre impresario takes a performer's agent round the show, now back in business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent' looks like the definition, since an operative is an agent; but it is wordplay, and the definition is the adjective 'working'.
explanation.definitionFit: Operative as an adjective means functioning or in force, as in 'the law is now operative'.

clue.text: Reward for man once incarcerated in Reading?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the statuette awarded at the Academy Awards
second meaning: the writer imprisoned in Reading Gaol in the 1890s

explanation.walkthrough: Reading is an English town, not the activity: Oscar Wilde served his sentence in its gaol and wrote The Ballad of Reading Gaol.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is a film-industry prize, and Oscar Wilde was the playwright jailed in Reading for gross indecency.

clue.text: Minor ruler and knight sat around fireplace

indicators.note: people who sit around something surround it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: KT is the abbreviation for a knight of an order
an ingle is a fireside, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: A petty king and his knight warm themselves by the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinglet is a petty king who rules a small or unimportant territory; the diminutive -let marks smallness.

clue.text: Minister returning to probe murder and wicked exploitation

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so this piece is pushed inside the next

parts.note: to slay is to kill

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, Reverend, is the title of a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A clergyman comes back to investigate a killing and some wicked doings, like a cosy crime novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavery is the ownership and forced labour of people, the most extreme and evil form of exploitation.

clue.text: Polish cad attending social event

parts.note: a heel is a dishonourable man
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A Polish bounder turns up at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests the nationality, but it is the noun polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Heelball is a mixture of wax and lampblack used by shoemakers to polish heels and soles, and for brass rubbings.

clue.text: Christian Union chaps grabbing converted cheat, one preparing for baptism

indicators.note: to grab is to take hold of, so the first piece wraps round what it grabs

parts.note: CU is the usual abbreviation for a student Christian Union

indicators.note: something converted is changed into another form, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A student Christian group takes in a reformed cheat who is getting ready to be baptised.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged cheat goes between the C and U, and MEN follows. 'Converted' fits the religious surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechumen is a convert receiving instruction in Christian doctrine before being baptised.

clue.text: Fighter in hospital holding people

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a san is a sanatorium, a hospital for convalescents
a race is a people of shared descent

explanation.surface: A wounded soldier in hospital is surrounded by people.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European term for the Muslim warriors fought by the Crusaders.

clue.text: Sudden chilly weather brings diseases — sleep!

parts.note: colds are minor viral illnesses
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Winter weather brings sniffles, so the cure is to go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold snap is a brief, abrupt spell of freezing temperatures.

clue.text: Stuff disappearing — discarded old meat

indicators.note: what is discarded is thrown away, so this letter leaves the word

parts.note: something disappearing is going
O is the abbreviation for old
ham is cured pork

explanation.surface: Food is vanishing and stale meat has been thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the O from GOING, then add HAM. 'Stuff' is the noun for cloth, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven fabric, and gingham is a checked cotton cloth.

clue.text: Girl in charge of gripping performance of many stars

indicators.note: to grip is to hold tightly, so the first pieces wrap around what follows

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
an act is a turn on stage

explanation.surface: A young woman runs a show featuring a huge cast of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests showbiz celebrities, but the definition is astronomical.
explanation.definitionFit: Galactic means relating to a galaxy, a vast system containing billions of stars.

clue.text: Diplomat worries about government's latest measures

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: cares are anxieties

indicators.note: the latest of something comes at the end, so the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of government

explanation.surface: An ambassador frets over the latest policies coming from the government.
explanation.walkthrough: The T goes inside CARES after its first letter. 'Measures' looks like government policy, but it is units of area.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectares are metric units of land area, each ten thousand square metres, so they are measures.

clue.text: You'll be sat puzzling, no question!

indicators.note: puzzling over something means working the pieces into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A confident prediction that the solver will be stuck staring at this crossword, without a doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic expressions of agreement or certainty, an exclamation meaning 'without doubt'.

clue.text: Go wrong penetrating a blue island

indicators.note: to penetrate is to go inside, so this piece is placed within the next

parts.note: the sky is a blue, a sense of the word for the colour of the heavens
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A voyage goes awry somewhere in the blue sea near an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a small rocky island or reef, a word used mostly in Scotland.

clue.text: Educational paper full of clear beliefs

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the TES, formerly the Times Educational Supplement, is a British weekly for teachers
a net sum is what is cleared after deductions

explanation.surface: A teaching newspaper is packed with clearly stated principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenets are the principles or doctrines that a person or group holds to be true.

clue.text: Examination of vessel after end of voyages

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the final letter of voyages
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A ship is inspected once its journeys are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the vessel second. The nautical surface makes 'vessel' look like a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan is a close examination, whether a careful look or a medical imaging test.

clue.text: Number looking smart going round bottom part of ship

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the joined words are read from the end

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
sleek means smooth and well groomed

explanation.surface: A smartly turned-out number circles the lower deck of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelson is a beam fixed along the inside of a ship's keel to strengthen its floor.

clue.text: A person with a seat in vehicle gets one drink

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written
an MP holds a seat in Parliament
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A passenger with a seat in the car is handed a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'seat' is a parliamentary seat, not one in the car: a Member of Parliament holds a seat in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is a bitter red Italian aperitif, so it names a particular alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Chap eating duck and beef

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a chap is a man
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A man dines on roast duck and beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' is the slang verb meaning complain, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef and to moan are both informal verbs for grumbling or complaining.

clue.text: She's not quite what you'd expect!

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: what you would expect is normal

explanation.surface: A woman who turns out to be surprising, not what anyone predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for any woman's name; here it is Norma, also Bellini's opera heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female first name, so it can stand for 'she' in crossword usage.

clue.text: Asians primarily in East, we fancy!

definitions.text: Asians primarily in East, we fancy!

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Asians
the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A Western speaker guesses that certain Asians live mainly in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the people it describes are Asians living in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taiwanese are the people of Taiwan, an island nation in East Asia.
